title: Exceptional base change for towers and integral coefficients
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum: $k$ is the fixed algebraic closure of a finite field of characteristic $p$, and $\ell\ne p$ is prime [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite extension with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, and put $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y,Y'$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$, and let $v:Y'\to Y$ be any $k$-morphism [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Set $X'=X\times_Y Y'$ with projections $u:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$, so $fu=vf'$; use a compactification $f=pj$ and its pullback for $f'$ [def-cbc-compact-support-square]. No smoothness, flatness or properness of $v$ is assumed.

Use the ordinary derived categories of varying-coefficient strict towers and their uniformly bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategories $\Dctf(-_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$; normalization means that every derived reduction map is invertible [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]. Tower pullback is exact levelwise finite constant-ring pullback [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main, lem-sf-module-object-ordinary-coefficient-equivalence]; $Rf_{!,\bullet}$ and $f^!_\bullet$ mean [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels, det-sp-tower-gluing]. Finite exceptional base change means the counit transpose of inverse compact-support exchange [lem-pur-smb-extraordinary, det-sp-mixed-base-change]. At integral coefficients use $R_T=p_T^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], canonically the inverse limit of its finite quotient ring sheaves [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit]. The ambient category is the ordinary derived category of these module objects [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], $\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$ means bounded complexes with constructible cohomology in the finite constant local model sense [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and integral pullback is total derived module pullback [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Integral compact support is the separately derived compactification composite of [det-sp-integral-direct-image-tower]. Its smooth right adjoint is $H_f$ of [det-sp-integral-adjunction-bijection], restricted using the integral constructibility criterion [lem-sfb-internal-integral-criterion-forward, lem-sfb-internal-integral-criterion-reverse]. Then: 

1. extension by zero and proper base change give a natural isomorphism
   $\beta_{f,\bullet}:v_\bullet^*Rf_{!,\bullet}\xrightarrow{\sim}R(f')_{!,\bullet}u_\bullet^*$ of
   functors $\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)\to\Dctf(Y'_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$;
2. the transpose of $v_\bullet^*(\varepsilon_{f,\bullet})\circ\beta_{f,\bullet}^{-1}$ under
   the tower adjunction for $f'$ is a natural isomorphism
   $e_{f,\bullet}:u_\bullet^*f_\bullet^!\xrightarrow{\sim}(f')_\bullet^!v_\bullet^*$, whose level $n$
   is the finite exceptional base change $e_{f,\mathcal O_E/\ell^n}$, and which is
   compatible with the reduction maps (hence preserves normalized towers);
3. for $E=\Ql$ and $K\in\Dbc(Y,\Zl)$, $R\varprojlim$ of $e_{f,\bullet}(\operatorname{red}_YK)$ is
   an isomorphism $u_{\Zl}^*f^!_{\Zl}K\xrightarrow{\sim}(f')^!_{\Zl}v^*_{\Zl}K$ in
   $\Dbc(X',\Zl)$, the integral exceptional base change, that is, the transpose under
   $R(f')_{!,\Zl}\dashv(f')^!_{\Zl}$ of $v_{\Zl}^*(\varepsilon_{f,\Zl}(K))\circ\beta_{f,\Zl}(f^!_{\Zl}K)^{-1}$.
   Here the integral compact-support base change
   $\beta_{f,\Zl}(M):v_{\Zl}^*Rf_{!,\Zl}M\xrightarrow{\sim}R(f')_{!,\Zl}u_{\Zl}^*M$ ($M\in\Dbc(X,\Zl)$)
   is the coefficient transport of $\beta_{f,\bullet}(\operatorname{red}_XM)$: the unique map whose
   reduction, under the reduction identifications for $Rf_{!,\Zl}$ of
   [det-sp-integral-direct-image-tower] and the reconstruction counit for integral pullback, is
   $\beta_{f,\bullet}(\operatorname{red}_XM)$; it exists and is unique by the equivalence
   [det-sp-normalized-equivalence].

proof.text: Apply the existing tower_mate_evaluation_reduction theorem to obtain a,hb,hfinite and Laws. Retain these data and laws without altering the tower adjunctions or coefficient conventions.

Apply finite_mates_and_source_normalized. For each input K and level n, Laws.evaluation identifies evaluation of the actual mate, followed by targetComparison.hom, with sourceComparison.hom followed by the finiteMate. The latter and both comparisons are invertible. Cancel targetComparison to see that every evaluation of the mate is invertible. The calculus detects isomorphisms; transport through levelComparison and the realization equivalence, then reflect through the full ctf inclusion. Thus the actual tower mate is invertible.

The same finite criterion supplies normalization of U(a.right K) on normalized K. The tower mate is now an isomorphism. Naturality of every actual derived reduction conjugates the target reduction by the evaluated isomorphisms and the scalar image of the source isomorphism. Hence the target reduction is invertible. This proves both normalized conclusions without assuming evaluation is faithful on arbitrary morphisms.

For rank-one E and the stated residue-field invertibility, obtain the compatible IntegralData package. Form the natural isomorphism between reduced support/pullback composites using supportComparison, pullComparison, beta and their inverses. Pull this entire natural isomorphism back along the fully faithful reduction functor using whiskeringRight.preimageIso. The component formula is exactly exchangeReduction. Faithfulness proves uniqueness of the resulting integral beta.

Conjugate the tower mate by source and target. Its fully faithful preimage is reconstructed, so it is invertible. Unit naturality for reduction followed by total limit is precisely IsLimitRealization; this proves the actual unit/limit/inverse-unit reconstruction equation.

Use mateEquiv_counit to obtain beta_G followed by support of mate followed by the primed counit equals pullback of the unprimed counit. Reduce the analogous integral expression. The two supportComparison naturality squares, the counit equations in IntegralData, the source/target component formulas and naturality of tower beta reduce it to this tower equation. Faithfulness gives the integral counit identity. Cancel integral beta and apply injectivity of the primed adjunction Hom equivalence. The resulting equality identifies reconstructed with the specified integralTranspose, proving IntegralConclusion.
